parent_idea: Preprints with shorter titles collect more citations at two years because search engines retrieve them more often.

ideas.title: Abstract term coverage instead of title length
ideas.statement: Keep the goal (raise retrieval visibility) and change the mechanism: the coverage of query terms in the abstract, not the length of the title, is the lever.

materials.why: The association that the idea tries to explain by another mechanism.
The repairable variant already names term coverage.

mechanism.summary: Query-term coverage of the abstract drives the rank of a record in scholarly search.
mechanism.goal: Raise retrieval visibility of a preprint.

hypothesis.statement: Abstract term coverage predicts retrieval rank better than title length does.
hypothesis.false_if: Rank is unchanged when the abstract is rewritten for coverage.

test.one_line: Rewrite 200 abstracts for term coverage and lengthen 200 controls, then compare the paired rank change.
test.variable: retrieval rank of the same preprint
test.if_holds: The coverage rewrite gains rank and the length change does not.

queries: abstract term coverage retrieval rank preprint
prior_art.scope: OpenAlex and arXiv, documents dated before 2026-11-14, titles and abstracts.

closest_work.title: Abstract wording and retrieval in scholarly search
closest_work.what_differs: Observational on one engine; no paired rewrite of the same preprint.

prior_art.difference: The closest work is observational; the idea adds a paired intervention on the same preprints.

tool.name: pandas and a title-rewrite script
tool.access: local script of the T1 apparatus

ideas.teaches: Whether the lever is the title at all or the wording of the whole record, which decides where authors should act.

gains: Cheapest test, reuses the T1 apparatus.
costs: Needs consent-free rewriting of public records only.
uncertainties: Engines may weight titles more than abstracts.

ideas.title: News headline length applied to preprint titles
ideas.statement: Transfer the headline-length findings of news search to preprint titles in scholarly search.

analogy.corresponds: Both rank short text fields mostly by term match.
analogy.breaks: Scholarly engines also weight citation counts and venue; news engines weight recency.

ref.says: rank depends on matches of title terms

materials.why: Retrieval rank by title-term match is the shared mechanism.

mechanism.summary: Short text fields are ranked by exact term match, so a shorter field concentrates the match weight.
mechanism.goal: Increase the chance that a short text is retrieved.

hypothesis.statement: The match-weight effect measured for news headlines also holds for preprint titles.
hypothesis.false_if: Scholarly engines weight citation counts so heavily that title match no longer moves the rank.

test.one_line: Replay the headline experiment design on a sample of preprint titles in two scholarly engines.
test.variable: rank position under a fixed query
test.if_holds: Shorter titles rank higher at equal content.
test.if_fails: Rank is flat in title length once citations are held fixed.

queries: headline length retrieval news search preprint title
prior_art.scope: OpenAlex and arXiv, documents dated before 2026-11-14, titles and abstracts.

ideas.teaches: Whether the retrieval mechanism is general across text genres.

uncertainties: Engines differ in how much they weight citations.

ideas.title: Title-term matching in dataset search as a bridge
ideas.statement: Use the literature on query-title matching in dataset retrieval as an intermediate concept that links the idea to a neighbouring field.

ref.says: rank depends on matches of title terms

materials.why: Start of the bridge: title-term match drives rank.
End of the bridge: wording changes clicks, an intermediate step to citations.

mechanism.summary: Title wording changes click-through, which feeds usage and then citations.
mechanism.goal: Explain the link between titles and citations through usage.

hypothesis.statement: Click-through mediates the effect of title wording on citations.
hypothesis.false_if: Title wording changes clicks but citations do not follow clicks.

test.one_line: Mediation analysis of title wording, clicks and citations on public usage logs of one repository.
test.variable: indirect effect of wording on citations through clicks
test.if_holds: The indirect effect is clearly above zero.
test.if_fails: The indirect effect is zero or opposite.

prior_art.scope: OpenAlex and arXiv, documents dated before 2026-11-14, titles and abstracts.

closest_work.title: Clicks as a mediator of citations
closest_work.what_differs: Same bridge, applied to dataset titles only.

ideas.teaches: Whether usage is the missing link between retrieval and citations.

uncertainties: Logs may be too sparse for a mediation estimate.

ideas.title: Author title-crafting skill as the residual
ideas.statement: Explain the association that survives the journal adjustment by author-level skill in crafting titles.

materials.why: The residual association is the anomaly this idea tries to explain.

mechanism.summary: Authors who craft concise titles also craft clearer papers, which collect more citations.
mechanism.goal: Explain the residual association left after adjusting for journal.

hypothesis.statement: The residual association disappears when author identity is held fixed.
hypothesis.false_if: It persists inside authors who change title length between papers.

test.one_line: Author fixed-effects regression of citations on title length over 5000 multi-paper authors.
test.if_holds: The coefficient shrinks to about zero.

queries: author fixed effects title length citations
prior_art.scope: OpenAlex and arXiv, documents dated before 2026-11-14, titles and abstracts.

tool.name: pandas and a title-rewrite script
tool.access: local script of the T1 apparatus

ideas.teaches: Whether the association is a property of authors or of titles.

uncertainties: Disambiguation errors may bias the coefficient.

ideas.title: Longer titles gain in narrow fields
ideas.statement: Invert the hypothesis: in narrow fields, longer and more specific titles are retrieved more because they match precise queries.

materials.why: Its sign is the one being inverted.

mechanism.summary: Specific long titles match the rare terms of precise queries in narrow fields.
mechanism.goal: Find the field type where title length helps retrieval.

hypothesis.statement: The sign of the title-length effect reverses in fields with few papers.
hypothesis.false_if: The effect is negative in every field size.

test.one_line: Interaction of title length and field size in the retrieval rank model of T1.
test.if_holds: A positive interaction with field narrowness.

queries: title length narrow field retrieval sign reversal
prior_art.scope: OpenAlex only, one engine, documents dated before 2026-11-14; arXiv was not searched.

tool.name: pandas and a title-rewrite script
tool.access: local script of the T1 apparatus

ideas.teaches: Whether a single sign of the effect can be assumed across fields.

ranking.basis: Feasibility from verifiable elements, cheapest minimal test, and what each idea would teach for the next decision; scenarios, no score.

scenarios.if: The researcher wants the cheapest test of the retrieval mechanism.
scenarios.why: Its data, tool, time and compute are established and its test reuses the T1 apparatus.

scenarios.if: The researcher wants to understand the residual association first.
scenarios.why: It needs only public metadata but the time cost is not established.

scenarios.if: The researcher worries about work already done.
scenarios.why: Prior art says it exists: read it, do not redo it.

rejected.reason: Needs a headline dataset that is not at hand.
